frontier.action: Test content-addressed textual chunk+manifest representation for one small binary-semantic payload. Separate exact byte preservation in text encoding from the stronger requirement that a raw binary artifact itself exist at a consumer-visible path; reject any route needing a decoder executor when raw artifact materialization is part of the outcome.

Compare bounded text encoding candidates (hex/base64/content-addressed manifest) by Chat verifiability, conflict/idempotency, size overhead, quota fragility and reconstruction semantics; preserve zero-quota alternatives.
Extend proof-carrying bounded DAG only when an actual finite checker needs another exact operation; keep unsupported operations closed.

exact_next_action: Create an isolated role-local fixture containing a tiny binary-semantic byte sequence represented only as deterministic UTF-8 text chunks plus a manifest. Verify chunk IDs, ordering, length and whole-payload digest from the text representation; test malformed chunk/order/digest controls. Then classify two outcomes separately: semantic byte preservation/reconstruction specification versus raw binary file materialization. The first may pass within Chat-native text/CAS scope; the second must remain unresolved if it requires any external decoder or binary-write capability.
